## TL;DR

The macOS Hub QA implementation and its record remain in the current worktree. The requested `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed on tree `c089428d6b427ece90cd706ae6a6a37f0706cda3`. The human follow-up #1174 still has no signed-in Projects and Tasks results, so that acceptance criterion remains explicitly unverified and this task is not ready for a truthful handoff.

## Work and rationale

This QA pass built the Hub with Xcode using `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO` and its own DerivedData path, launched the app through LaunchServices with an isolated support directory, and drove the initial screens. The recorded run checked first-run empty state, discovery of a live local RepoOS server, addition and persistence of the discovered server after a healthy response, and rendering of the connected server's sign-in page. Captures were made for app windows only with `screencapture -l<windowid>`; no full-screen capture was taken. The QA record documents the paths exercised and the screens not reached.

The QA run found that an XCTest app host could write to the real Hub server registry when it ran without an explicit support-directory override. The fix resolves an isolated per-process temporary support directory for XCTest after honoring an explicit override, and removes that scratch directory on host termination. Cleanup failures are surfaced instead of swallowed. Table-driven directory-resolution coverage plus cleanup and error-propagation tests guard those cases. The QA record also discloses the one real registry write that occurred before this fix, because the prior registry selection was not captured and therefore cannot safely be reconstructed.

The report and QA record do not claim that every Hub feature was exercised. Local server discovery and the connected sign-in page establish that the app built, launched, discovered a server, connected, and rendered its web content. They do not establish that authenticated project/task screens work. Preserving that distinction keeps the verification record useful for review and gives the human follow-up a concrete target.

## Approaches tried

The app was built and launched using an isolated support directory. The app window and accessibility contents were inspected for the empty state, server-add flow, and connected web view. `xcodebuild test` was run with an isolated test-host registry after the storage issue was found; focused registry tests and the full XCTest suite passed in the QA session. A direct executable launch was also observed: a process started, but only menu-bar-sized windows appeared during the short observation window. This remains an unexplained edge case, not a confirmed crash. The normal LaunchServices launch did present a content window.

In this resumed session I re-read the latest review report and the engineering-round metadata, verified that the report draft existed, and ran `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` against the current tree. RepoOS reported the changed-path build, format, lint, branch-artifact, task-asset and UI smoke checks as passed; tests ran on the remote validation runner, and the overall result was `All checks passed`. UI-specific web checks and unrelated package checks were skipped by the declared changed-path plan. The check did not modify the worktree HEAD.

## Challenges and blockers

The connected server requires an authorized email-code sign-in before the Projects and Tasks views are available. Prior synthetic typing and clicks did not complete that flow. Human follow-up #1174 is the designated place to perform and record this verification, and the board currently has no result from that task. I did not attempt to bypass authentication or invent screen observations. Until #1174 records a result, the desired UX and acceptance criterion covering authenticated projects and tasks remain open.

Other areas were outside this run: discovery of a server that is not running, settings, the command palette, notifications, Dock badge behavior, and WebKit OAuth. The direct-executable launch behavior also needs a focused follow-up if that launch mode is expected to work. The original QA record accurately lists these limits.

## Key learnings

A successful sign-in-page render is evidence of connection and web rendering, not authenticated app functionality. Email-code entry that does not reach the authenticated page must stay an explicit gap. XCTest app-host processes also need their own storage boundary, since tests can otherwise mutate a developer's real app-support data. Finally, a passing scoped check verifies the current source tree but cannot provide missing human observations; those are separate evidence requirements.
